subject: Temporary priority lane request for marquee event — SLA/throughput exception
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna.li@wavefrontmedia.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Aug 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary priority lane request for marquee event — SLA/throughput exception

Hi Jonas,

We're launching a global marketing push the week of Aug 21 and expect a concentrated spike in API traffic for our personalization and chat features. Our engineering team ran projections and attached a Q3 traffic projection (event_traffic_projection.xlsx).

Short version of the ask: can Redwood provision a short-term priority lane (higher burst quota + preferential queuing / fairness carveout) for the period Aug 21–Aug 28 to keep p99 latency under 350ms for our top-tier endpoints? We understand this is an exception to the standard rate limits and are open to scoped limits, runbooks, and an additional commitment if needed.

We need to confirm by EOD Aug 10 so our partner integrations can be validated.

Thanks,
Anna Li
Director of Integrations
Wavefront Media

Attachments: event_traffic_projection.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@wavefrontmedia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary priority lane request for marquee event — SLA/throughput exception

Hi Anna — thanks for the heads up and the projection. This is the sort of spike we've seen in other media launches and we can usually accommodate with a short-term policy change plus a temporary priority token pool.

Proposal (quick):
- Window: Aug 21 00:00 UTC — Aug 28 23:59 UTC
- Priority lane: dedicated token pool for Wavefront traffic capped at 12k concurrent tokens (tunable)
- Latency target: p99 <= 350ms for routed requests to your pinned model variants; we will monitor and notify on breaches
- Fairness: during contention we'll route Wavefront requests to the priority pool first, but fallback to standard pool if capacity is exhausted — we can also set a hard cap to avoid affecting other customers
- Duration and rollback: automatic rollback after Aug 28 unless we agree to extend

Marissa, Ben — can you confirm operational feasibility and the commercial terms (credits, surcharge, or short-term uplift)? Anna — if that looks ok, we can draft an SLA addendum and a short runbook for your SREs.

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Anna Li <anna.li@wavefrontmedia.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Aug 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary priority lane request for marquee event — SLA/throughput exception

Hi all — operational notes from infra/CS: we can spin up a priority token pool scoped to Wavefront for that window. A few points to lock down:

- Hard cap vs soft cap: recommend a soft cap (12k) with alerts and a safety hard cap (18k) so other customers are protected.
- Telemetry: we'll enable a dedicated dashboard (per-route latency, token utilization, queueing time) and 1-min alerts for p95/p99 breaches.
- KV cache warming: to hit p99 targets we should preload prefix caches for the top 200k active keys — Anna, can you share the top endpoints or a short seed list?
- Rollback triggers: sustained p99 > 450ms for 15m or >550ms for 5m will auto-disable the priority pool and revert to baseline routing.

I can prepare the runbook and take point on the monitoring. We'll need a signed addendum that authorizes the temporary capacity and the emergency rollback behavior.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Inference Ops
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_runbook_outline.md (text, referenced)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@wavefrontmedia.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Aug 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary priority lane request for marquee event — SLA/throughput exception

Anna — happy to work through the commercial side. Options we typically offer:
1) One-week priority addendum at list uplift (no credits)
2) One-week priority addendum in exchange for modest committed minimum (short-term revenue commit)
3) Credit offset if you take a 3-month reserved capacity commitment after the event

Given your timeline, option 1 is the fastest to approve; option 3 gives you a lower unit cost longer term. I'll draft a short addendum and pricing appendix and can get legal to do an expedited review — please confirm which option you prefer.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Accounts
ben@redwood.com

Attachment: pricing_appendix_draft.pdf (pdf, 18KB)

From: Anna Li <anna.li@wavefrontmedia.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Aug 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary priority lane request for marquee event — SLA/throughput exception

Thanks everyone — option 1 works for us (fastest). We've reviewed the runbook outline offline and attached a signed PDF of the addendum; Ops will share the top endpoints tomorrow morning to assist cache warming.

We'll need the dashboard and 1-min alerts enabled at least 24 hours before the window. Please send the DocuSign link for the addendum and the HubSpot deal so our procurement team can track it.

Anna Li
Director of Integrations
Wavefront Media

Attachments: signed_priority_addendum.pdf (pdf, 65KB)
